paragraphs: As of Friday, October 2, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq enters payroll Friday with a resilient tape but an unusually difficult rates backdrop. The Nasdaq Composite recovered from a sharp intraday selloff on Thursday to finish 0.04% higher, while the S&P 500 gained 0.20%. The important move was underneath the indexes: the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield surged as high as 5.342%, its highest level since 2002, before retreating as the session progressed. That reversal allowed technology shares to stabilize, while strong AI-related demand signals around Micron and record Korean semiconductor exports continued to support the structural semiconductor story.

The counterweight is that the long end of the Treasury market remains the dominant valuation risk for Nasdaq. Oil also jumped more than 4% Thursday, with Brent settling at $102.31, after reports of additional U.S. military deployments to the Middle East and China's suspension of fuel-product exports added to supply concerns. At the same time, Fed officials have leaned against an immediate October hike after softer inflation, making today's employment report especially important: a moderate labor reading could reinforce the recent easing in near-term Fed expectations, while a strong payroll/wage combination could send yields back toward Thursday's highs. No reliable Nasdaq-100 futures quote available before the 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff was used.
watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the best Nasdaq scenario is a payroll report that shows orderly labor-market cooling, keeps unemployment contained, and pulls the 10-year decisively away from Thursday's 5.34% extreme while semiconductor leadership remains firm. The more dangerous scenario is a strong jobs/wages print that restarts the long-end selloff, especially if crude stays above $100 or geopolitical headlines push it higher. A superficially weak jobs number is not automatically bullish either: if unemployment rises sharply enough to trigger growth fears, lower yields may not translate cleanly into higher technology stocks.
